premise_result.summary: 17 premises extracted from the inherited plan and executed against disk at d81cb3d. 16 TRUE, 1 FALSE, 0 UNDECIDABLE. Full table: .dev-flow/2026-07-31-batch-74/00-measurements.md section 1.
premise_result.P14_FALSE: THE LOAD-BEARING FALSE PREMISE. The plan and the backlog state OB-4's cost as a flat '988 B/entry'. MEASURED: 140.1 B/entry (_modifications_lines) and 126.1 B/entry (_checklist_lines) at an 8-byte run, and the cost is LINEAR IN THE ENTRY'S BYTE-RUN LENGTH (~ 92 + 6*run bytes), because _format_bytes renders 3 chars per byte into TWO cells per row. 988 B/entry is simply the value at a ~149-byte run. CONSEQUENCE: a row-count cap alone does NOT bound resident memory - _format_bytes (:538-556) has no limit and MF_RUN_LENGTH_CEILING = 1_048_576 (changes/io.py:232) lets ONE row cost ~6 MiB, so a 200-row cap bounds the table at ~1.2 GB. This directly falsifies the plan's Inc-1/Inc-2 sketch and forced design ruling D-1.
premise_result.P15_TRUE_WITH_ADAPTATION: batch-65's _addendum_lines shape transfers in three of its four mechanisms (admission counters with the cap applied AT admission; traversal NOT terminated on saturation so the notice can state a true dropped count; one truncation notice naming what was cut). The fourth - format only AFTER the membership test - has NO analogue: the addendum has a region-membership discriminator and these two producers have none, since every entry is a row by definition.
premise_result.P6_TRUE: The plan's load-bearing design constraint is confirmed at the source: emit() (:2215-2217) calls budget.consume(...) only - it ACCOUNTS, NEVER GATES. The sole budget.fits(...) gate is _hexdump_section:1455. So emit(_modifications_lines(...)) at :2243 has fully materialised the producer before consume is reached, and charging these tables to _ByteBudget would close F4 while leaving OB-4 completely untouched.
